import SystemE
import Book1.Prop03.Main
import Book1.Prop05.Main
import Book1.Prop19.Main

namespace Elements.Book1

/-- The vertex-`a` triangle inequality: in triangle `a b c`, the two sides meeting at `a`
    (namely `ba` and `ac`) together exceed the opposite side `bc`.  This is exactly Euclid's
    Prop. 1.20 argument (Prop. 1.3 construction, Prop. 1.5 isosceles base-angles, Prop. 1.19
    greater-angle-subtends-greater-side), isolated so the "similarly we can show" sentences can
    reuse it for the other two vertices. -/
theorem helper_1_20_triangle_ineq (a b c : Point) (AB BC AC : Line)
    (h : formTriangle a b c AB BC AC) : |(b─a)| + |(a─c)| > |(b─c)| := by
  euclid_intros
  euclid_apply (extend_point_longer AB b a (c─a)) as d'
  euclid_apply (proposition_3 a d' a c AB AC) as d
  euclid_apply (line_from_points d c) as DC
  euclid_apply (extend_point AC a c) as e
  euclid_apply (proposition_5 a d c d' e AB DC AC)
  euclid_assert (between b a d)
  euclid_assert (∠ b:c:d > ∠ a:d:c)
  euclid_assert (∠ b:c:d > ∠ b:d:c)
  euclid_apply (proposition_19 b c d BC DC AB)
  euclid_finish

end Elements.Book1
